newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end off lows on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end off lows on bargain hunting.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks ended down on lacklustre trading, but off their intraday lows, and the Second Board staged a recovery to end in positive territory, fuelled by bargain hunting, dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 11.24 points down to 1,188.45, while the small-capitalised Second Board index was up 2.33 to 545.06.
"There has been quite a bit of bargain hunting in the last half of the day," said a trader at a local brokerage house.
"Much of the gains were on small-cap stocks. Fifty-three percent of the gainers were on the Second Board," he said.
Volume was low with 154 million shares traded. Losers edged out gainers by 294 to 268, with 168 stocks remaining unchanged.

"The Second Board is drifting between its support and resistance levels, consequently there has been some bargain hunting," the dealer said. "The CI (Composite Index) was also off its low (of 1,181.01 for the day), but the bargain hunting here was not as great," he said.

Technology Resources, among the day's most actively-traded stocks, was unchanged at 4.52 ringgit after hitting a low of 4.44. Traders said the company's cellular telephone operations were facing severe billing problems resulting in lost revenue.
